OverviewFeaturesUse casesPricingTradeoffsCompatibilityFAQ

What is Cursor?

AI-native code editor built as a VS Code fork, designed around agentic multi-file editing rather than line completion. Your extensions, settings and keybindings carry over, but the AI is the centre of the interface rather than an add-on.

Best for

Heavy agent-driven work across a whole codebase.

Main features

  • Composer/Agent for autonomous multi-file changes
  • full-codebase indexing and semantic search
  • Tab completion model tuned for multi-line edits
  • inline edit (Cmd+K)
  • Bugbot automated code review
  • model selection across frontier providers
  • BYO API key option
  • .cursorrules project instructions
  • terminal command generation
  • background agents.

Practical use cases

  • Large multi-file refactors
  • implementing a feature across several modules from a description
  • understanding an unfamiliar codebase through semantic search
  • generating and running tests
  • migrating a framework version.

Who is it for?

  • Professional developers, startups, and engineering teams willing to change editor for a stronger agent.

Pricing, free access & limits

Per-seat subscription with included usage credits; BYO API key optional

Plans described in the source

Hobby free with limited completions and requests. Pro $20/mo. Pro+ $60/mo. Ultra $200/mo. Business $40/user/mo with admin controls, centralised billing, SSO and privacy mode enforcement. Enterprise custom. Higher tiers buy larger included usage pools; heavy use beyond the pool is metered or throttled.

Free plan

Yes - Hobby tier free with limited AI completions and chat.

Free trial

Yes - a two-week Pro trial is typically offered on signup.

Usage limits to consider

Each tier includes a usage allowance for premium model requests; exceeding it slows requests or incurs charges. The free Hobby tier restricts context to limited scope and uses a basic model.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • The strongest agent experience among IDE-based tools
  • codebase indexing makes context handling noticeably better than extension-based assistants
  • migration from VS Code is effectively free
  • Tab model for multi-line edits is excellent.

Limitations to consider

  • Twice the entry price of GitHub Copilot
  • requires switching editors, which some teams will not do
  • usage-credit accounting is opaque and users report unexpected charges (Trustpilot ratings reflect billing complaints)
  • no free tier of real substance
  • less mature enterprise governance than GitHub.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • macOS, Windows, Linux (standalone editor)
  • Cursor CLI

Languages

  • All mainstream programming languages

API access

No public API for the editor; supports BYO provider API keys

Integrations and exports

  • Full VS Code extension marketplace compatibility
  • Git/GitHub
  • MCP servers
  • Slack and Linear (background agents)

Evaluation notes

Cursor reshaped its Teams tiers in mid-2026, so older cost comparisons are stale. Many developers run both Cursor and Copilot and switch by task - the tools are not mutually exclusive.

What limits should I check before using Cursor?

Each tier includes a usage allowance for premium model requests; exceeding it slows requests or incurs charges. The free Hobby tier restricts context to limited scope and uses a basic model.
